arxiv-2410-08554.title: Integrated adaptive coherent LiDAR for 4D bionic vision
arxiv-2410-08554.creator: Ruixuan Chen 1† , Yichen Wu 1† , Ke Zhang 2† , Chuxin Liu 3† , Yikun Chen 2 , Wencan Li 1 , Bitao Shen 1 , Zhaoxi Chen 2 , Hanke Feng 2 , Zhangfeng Ge 4 , Yan Zhou 4 , Zihan Tao 1 , Weihan Xu 3 , Yimeng Wang 1 , Pengfei Cai 6 , Dong Pan 6 , Haowen Shu 1,5∗ , Linjie Zhou 3∗ , Cheng Wang 2∗ and Xingju
arxiv-2410-08554.description: Abstract Abstract Light detection and ranging (LiDAR) is a ubiquitous tool to provide precise spatial awareness in various perception environments. A bionic LiDAR that can mimic human-like vision by adaptively gazing at selected regions of interest within a broad field of view is crucial to achieve high-resolution imaging in an energy-saving and cost-effective manner.

arxiv-2510-01163.title: How Does the Pretraining Distribution Shape In-Context Learning? Task Selection, Generalization, and Robustness
arxiv-2510-01163.creator: Waïss Azizian, Ali Hasan
arxiv-2510-01163.description: Abstract The emergence of in-context learning (ICL) in large language models (LLMs) remains poorly understood despite its consistent effectiveness, enabling models to adapt to new tasks from only a handful of examples. To clarify and improve these capabilities, we characterize how the statistical properties of the pretraining distribution (e.g., tail behavior, coverage) shape ICL on numerical tasks.

arxiv-2511-19794.title: When +1% Is Not Enough: A Paired Bootstrap Protocol for Evaluating Small Improvements
arxiv-2511-19794.creator: Du Wenzhang
arxiv-2511-19794.description: Abstract Recent machine learning papers often report one–two percentage point improvements from a single run. These gains are measured on standard benchmarks and are highly sensitive to random seeds, data ordering, and implementation details, yet are rarely accompanied by uncertainty estimates or significance tests. It is therefore unclear when a reported “+1–2%” reflects a real algorithmic advance versus noise.

arxiv-2512-01583.title: Fixed Points in Quantum Metric Spaces: A Structural Advantage over Fuzzy Frameworks
arxiv-2512-01583.creator: Nicola Fabiano
arxiv-2512-01583.description: Abstract We prove an existence and uniqueness theorem for fixed points of contraction maps in the framework of quantum metric spaces, where distinguishability is defined by the L 2 L^{2} norm: d Q ​ ( ψ 1 , ψ 2 ) = ‖ ψ 1 − ψ 2 ‖ d_{Q}(\psi_{1},\psi_{2})=\|\psi_{1}-\psi_{2}\| .

pmc-11302083.title: Effects of pain exacerbation on postural control in women with patellofemoral pain during single leg squat: a cross-sectional study
pmc-11302083.creator: Ali Yalfani, Fatemeh Ahadi, Mohamadreza Ahmadi
pmc-11302083.description: BackgroundThe center of pressure (COP) excursion parameters are recognized as risk factors for the etiology and development of patellofemoral pain (PFP). The purpose of the present study measures the effect of pain exacerbation on COP excursion, and the correlation between pain intensity and COP excursion in women with PFP during single leg squat (SLS).

pmc-11392932.title: Hybrid lipid-AuNP clusters as highly efficient SERS substrates for biomedical applications
pmc-11392932.creator: Jacopo Cardellini, Caterina Dallari, Ilaria De Santis, Lorenzo Riccio, Costanza Ceni, Amelia Morrone, Martino Calamai, Francesco Saverio Pavone, Caterina Credi, Costanza Montis, Debora Berti
pmc-11392932.description: Although Surface Enhanced Raman Scattering (SERS) is widely applied for ultrasensitive diagnostics and imaging, its potential is largely limited by the difficult preparation of SERS tags, typically metallic nanoparticles (NPs) functionalized with Raman-active molecules (RRs), whose production often involves complex synthetic approaches, low colloidal stability and poor reproducibility.

pmc-11395814.title: New Advances in Metastatic Urothelial Cancer: A Narrative Review on Recent Developments and Future Perspectives
pmc-11395814.creator: Elena Tonni, Marco Oltrecolli, Marta Pirola, Cyrielle Tchawa, Sara Roccabruna, Elisa D’Agostino, Rossana Matranga, Claudia Piombino, Stefania Pipitone, Cinzia Baldessari, Francesca Bacchelli, Massimo Dominici, Roberto Sabbatini, Maria Giuseppa Vitale
pmc-11395814.description: A peer-reviewed research article from Europe PMC (2024). The standard of care for advanced or metastatic urothelial carcinoma (mUC) was historically identified with platinum-based chemotherapy. Thanks to the advances in biological and genetic knowledge and technologies, new therapeutic agents have emerged in this setting recently: the immune checkpoint inhibitors and the fibroblast growth factor receptor inhibitors as the target therapy for patients harboring alterations in the fibroblast growth factor receptor (FGFR) pathway.

pmc-11591676.title: A Metal-Organic Framework-Based Colorimetric Sensor Array for Transcutaneous CO2 Monitoring via Lensless Imaging
pmc-11591676.creator: Syed Saad Ahmed, Jingjing Yu, Wei Ding, Sabyasachi Ghosh, David Brumels, Songxin Tan, Laxmi Raj Jaishi, Amirhossein Amjad, Xiaojun Xian
pmc-11591676.description: Transcutaneous carbon dioxide (TcPCO2) monitoring provides a non-invasive alternative to measuring arterial carbon dioxide (PaCO2), making it valuable for various applications, such as sleep diagnostics and neonatal care. However, traditional transcutaneous monitors are bulky, expensive, and pose risks such as skin burns.

pmc-11610740.title: Impact of COVID-19 Pandemic on Emergency Department Visits for Opioid Use Disorder Across University of California Health Centers
pmc-11610740.creator: Matthew Heshmatipour, Ding Quan Ng, Emily Yi-Wen Truong, Jianwei Zheng, Alexandre Chan, Yun Wang
pmc-11610740.description: IntroductionCoronavirus 2019 (COVID-19) has had a devastating impact on mental health and access to addiction treatment in the United States, including in California, which resulted in the highest rates of emergency department visits (ED) for opioid poisoning in 2020. As California slowly returns to pre-pandemic normalcy, it remains uncertain whether the rates of opioid-related events have slowed down over time.

pmc-11618443.title: Printed Potentiometric Ammonium Sensors for Agriculture Applications
pmc-11618443.creator: Anju Toor, Payton Goodrich, Tyler L Anthony, Claire Beckstoffer, Haeshini Jegan, Whendee L Silver, Ana Claudia Arias
pmc-11618443.description: Ammonium (NH4+) concentration is critical to both nutrient availability and nitrogen (N) loss in soil ecosystems but can be highly variable across spatial and temporal scales. For this reason, effectively informing agricultural practices such as fertilizer management and understanding of mechanisms of soil N loss require sensor technologies to monitor ammonium concentrations in real time.

pmc-12562314.title: Impact of High Hydrostatic Pressure, Ultrasound, and Pulsed Electric Field in Beverages Fermentation: A Review of Nutritional, Functional, and Sensory Aspects and the Future
pmc-12562314.creator: Sebastián Pizarro-Oteíza, Fernando Salazar, Romina Cea, Oscar Cavieres, Maninder Meenu, Eduardo Puértolas, Barbaros Özer
pmc-12562314.description: This review evaluated the impact of emerging non-thermal technologies, such as high hydrostatic pressure (HHP), ultrasound (US), and pulsed electric fields (PEF), on the properties of fermented beverages. According to the information gathered, HHP improves cellular integrity and antioxidant activity of beverages, while US enhances nutrient release and improves the nutritional profile by increasing peptide content and cell viability.

pmc-12695959.title: Mothers’ and Fathers’ Personality, Infants’ Anger Proneness, and Responsive Parenting
pmc-12695959.creator: Grazyna Kochanska, Lilly C. Bendel-Stenzel, Danming An
pmc-12695959.description: Parenting in infancy is immensely important for children’s development and therefore, contributors to varying quality of early parenting have been extensively studied. Among those, parents’ personality and its links with parenting have attracted intense interest, but factors that may affect those associations, including characteristics of the child, particularly in father-infant relationships, remain poorly understood (Taraban & Shaw, 2018).

pmc-13002538.title: Mapping System–Assisted Bipolar Radiofrequency Ablation for the Treatment of Ventricular Tachycardia Associated With Ventricular Aneurysm
pmc-13002538.creator: Xiangzhi Kong, Mingxin Gao, Chengxiong Gu, Haiyang Li, Yang Yu
pmc-13002538.description: BackgroundThe management of malignant ventricular tachycardia (VT) in the aftermath of a myocardial infarction is a complex undertaking, particularly in cases accompanied by left ventricular aneurysm (LVA). It is frequently the case that conventional unipolar radiofrequency catheter ablation (RFCA) is inadequate.Case SummaryA 50-year-old male patient with a medical history of myocardial infarction presented with recurrent VT due to a LVA.

There are several limitations to clinical care.

pmc-13202921.title: Spatial disparities and dynamic evolution of health human resources in primary healthcare institutions in China: a study from the perspective of aggregation degree
pmc-13202921.creator: Jiaxin Yin, Bingxue Ma, Yun Nie, Tianqi Wang
pmc-13202921.description: BackgroundAs a critical component of universal health coverage, the spatial distribution of human resources in primary healthcare has attracted sustained policy attention worldwide. As the world’s largest developing country, China’s experience provides an important setting for examining the spatial distribution and dynamic evolution of the primary healthcare workforce.

pmc-13264608.creator: Lorenz Schiessl, Anne Herrmann, Richard-Felix Kraus, Viktoria Kimmerling, Johanna Rosenberger, Cynthia Kohl, Martin Georg Kees, Alexander Leonhard Leibold

pmc-13296267.title: Betanin from Beta vulgaris Attenuates Complete Freund’s Adjuvant-Induced Inflammatory Pain: Integrated Preclinical and In Silico Insights
pmc-13296267.creator: Ahmed Massoud, Amina E. Essawy, Mohammed A. Alfredan, Ashraf M. Abdel-Moneim, Rehab A. Gomaa, Sherine Abdel Salam
pmc-13296267.description: Background/Objectives: Betanin (BET), a prominent phytochemical mainly derived from Beta vulgaris, exhibits strong anti-inflammatory and antioxidant activities owing to its distinctive chemical structure. Nevertheless, its potential analgesic effect in the context of inflammatory pain remains insufficiently explored. Accordingly, this study investigated the analgesic effects of BET in a complete Freund’s adjuvant (CFA)-induced rat model of inflammatory pain.

pmc-13358477.title: A retrospective study comparing T3 ganglionectomy and R4 sympathicotomy for reducing compensatory hyperhidrosis in primary palmar hyperhidrosis
pmc-13358477.creator: Ji Hoon Kim, Duk Hwan Moon, Sungsoo Lee, Beatrice Chia-Hui Shih

pmc-13378295.title: Maternal biological aging from pregnancy through four years postpartum with disrupted recovery by subsequent pregnancy
pmc-13378295.creator: Laura Etzel, Patricia Garrett-Peters, Qiaofeng Ye, Abner T. Apsley, Aaliya Ahamed, John T. Kozlosky, Christopher R. Chiaro, Lorrie Schmid, Victoria K. Lee, Cathi Propper, Roger Mills-Koonce, Sarah J. Short, Idan Shalev
pmc-13378295.description: A peer-reviewed research article from Europe PMC (2026). SummaryPregnancy has been proposed as a biological “stress test” that may transiently accelerate maternal biological aging, followed by partial recovery postpartum, yet longitudinal evidence remains limited. This longitudinal study followed 130 women at mid to late pregnancy, 6–9 months postpartum, and 36–43 months postpartum, to characterize nonlinear changes in markers of biological aging, including telomere length, epigenetic aging measures, and pace of aging derived from saliva samples.

pmc-13639699.title: Generative AI Needs a Pilot: Positioning Advanced Practice Nurses as the “Human-in-the-Loop” for Primary Care Safety
pmc-13639699.creator: Takeshi Miura, Tomohiko Takahashi, Kazumi Kubota
pmc-13639699.description: Generative artificial intelligence (GenAI) is increasingly integrated into primary care, supporting documentation, clinical summaries, and patient-facing communication. While its potential to reduce cognitive workload is widely recognized, GenAI introduces a safety paradox: as outputs become more fluent, inaccuracies such as hallucinations and omissions may become harder to detect.

pmc-13673851.title: Huangjing Jiangzhi Granules Ameliorate Nonalcoholic Fatty Liver Disease by Activating the FOXA1-DERL1 Regulatory Axis to Suppress Lipid Accumulation, Endoplasmic Reticulum Stress, and Apoptosis
pmc-13673851.creator: Dongyu Xie, Yunqing Wu, Jiawei Jiang, Lu Xu, Xueqin Sun, Jun Ouyang, Biao Xi, Dongliang Zhang, Haina Xie
pmc-13673851.description: Nonalcoholic fatty liver disease (NAFLD) is an emerging health issue worldwide. It involves intrahepatic lipid accumulation that is potentially deleterious. Traditional Chinese Medicine called Huangjing Jiangzhi (HJJZ) granules holds promise for NAFLD treatment. This study explored the mechanism by which HJJZ granules improve NAFLD in male C57BL/6 mice and oleic acid-induced HepG2 cells.
